wl-corrected-sums: Three Lean definitions give G: Formalism.Gz (the sum over 1 <= n <= floor(y) of Lambda(n)(y/n - 1)), Formalism.HC.An.G (the same with max(y/n - 1, 0)) and Deduction.G (the sum over 0 <= n <= floor(y)); UpperTheory.Comparison₂.Gz_eq shows that they agree for every real y. The twisted sums are Formalism.HC.An.gChi and Deduction.Gchi, which agree on primitive characters (UpperTheory.Comparison₂.gChi_eq). Both are defined for every Dirichlet character: An.gChi returns G for the trivial character of any modulus, and Deduction.Gchi returns the twisted sum minus y log y plus (1 + gamma)y for it. Only the trivial character modulo 1 occurs in the chapter, and there all of them are G. L(s, chi) is Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction, which for the character modulo 1 is riemannZeta; Mathlib gives riemannZeta a finite nonzero value at s = 1.
wl-character-family: Deduction.CharFamily has an index type with a Fintype instance, moduli N i, characters chi i, weights a i with a_pos, and the field adm: N i = 1 or chi i is nontrivial. Deduction.Gm F is the weighted Chebyshev sum, computed with Deduction.Gchi, and Deduction.zeroSet F is the zero set.
wl-level: A primitive character is Formalism.HC.PChar, a structure holding N, a Dirichlet character modulo N and a proof that it is primitive; the trivial one is PChar.one, at N = 1, and the conjugate is PChar.inv. A level is Formalism.HC.Level, which extends Formalism.HC.KSet (the finite set KEPT, one_mem, inv_mem, and the optional exceptional character psK with psK_spec: psK lies in KEPT, is odd and has real values) by the natural number o.
wl-weighted-sum: Formalism.HC.Level.Gm adds Formalism.Gz to the sum, over KEPT with PChar.one removed (Level.Nt), of Level.wt psi times the real part of An.gChi. Level.wt psi is 1 when psK = some psi and (3o + 1)^(-1) otherwise.
wl-cyclic-level: Level.cyc psi is Level.ofSub applied to the subgroup of characters modulo psi.N generated by psi.chi: its set is the image of that subgroup under PChar.of, which takes a character to the primitive character inducing it; psK is none; and o is the cardinality of the subgroup. Level.mem_cyc proves that psi lies in K_psi, and closure under conjugation is PChar.of_inv. The notation G_psi is the book's. The count of the elements of K_psi in the paragraph after the definition is not used.
wl-laplace-character: The Mellin formulas are mellin_Gchi_of_ne_one and mellin_Gchi_modOne, for Re s > 1, as integrals over (1, infinity) against y^(-s-1); poleData_change converts them to the Laplace form. Part (2) is poleData_char, built from poleData_abstract applied to f = L(s, chi) with k = 0, or with k = 1 to the function equal to (s - 1)zeta(s) away from s = 1 and to 1 at s = 1. It produces a function on C that equals the Laplace transform for Re s > 2 (the statement used later), is analytic at every rho != 0 with L(rho, chi) != 0, and has principal part m(-1/(rho(rho - 1)))/(s - rho) at every rho != 0, where m is the analytic order of f (logDeriv_local) and m = 0 exactly when L(rho, chi) != 0. The meromorphic extension in the text is this function away from the poles.
wl-pole-data: Deduction.PoleData has the fields meas, growth (item 1), laplace (item 2), pos and iso (item 3), diff (item 4) and pole (item 5). The field iso says that every point of the open right half-plane has a punctured neighbourhood disjoint from Z.
wl-pole-data-family: The plan listed this as a standard result, citing Ingham and Davenport for the classical computation. The Lean proves it in full from Mathlib's continuation of Dirichlet L-functions and their nonvanishing on Re s >= 1, and the deduction from Lemma wl-laplace-character is short, so the text gives the proof. The Lean statement records only that the residue c is nonzero, and real and positive at real points; the formula c = -S/(rho(rho - 1)) is the one in its proof. Phi_F is the sum of (a_i/2)(Phi_1 + Phi_2), where Phi_1 and Phi_2 come from poleData_char for chi_i and its inverse; the conjugation identities are Gchi_conj and LFunction_conj, which says L(conj s, chi^(-1)) = conj L(s, chi).
wl-window-hypothesis: Deduction.WindowHypU. The family version Deduction.WindowHyp is the same condition in the variable y = e^u, on [Y, Y^(1 + delta)] with the weight y^(-theta - 1); windowHypU_of_windowHyp converts one into the other.
wl-kernel-tails: The constants are those of landau_tails: l = 2 + 6/delta, M = l(1 + delta), sigma = M(2 + l), k = ceil((1 + delta/2) sigma U) and C_1 = e/(sigma - 2 - l) + 1/(sigma - 2 + l). The split of the exponential is landau_tails_chernoff, and the comparison of e^x a^(-k-1) with sigma^(-k) is landau_tails_pow.
wl-coefficient-bound: This is landau_window_key. The integral inequality is landau_window_ineq, the formula for the coefficients as integrals is landau_coeff (through iteratedDeriv_laplace, differentiation under the integral), and t^k e^(-t)/k! <= 1 is landau_kernel_max. The constant is C = 2 + 2 C_0 |C_1|.
wl-nearest-pole: The lemma combines landau_dichotomy, which chooses between a real nearest point and a disc about sigma free of Z, with landau_nearest, which moves the base point vertically to a point with a unique nearest point of Z. landau_finite gives the finiteness of Z in closed discs inside the half-plane.
wl-pole-coefficients: Part (1) is landau_cauchy, proved with Mathlib's bound on cauchyPowerSeries; M is the mean of |Phi| on the circle of radius r'. Part (2) is landau_pole_asym, which subtracts the principal part and applies landau_cauchy.
wl-landau-window: The hypothesis theta < 1 is not used in the proof. The step Re rho <= 2 is landau_pole_re_le, and the final contradiction is landau_window_contra, which applies landau_growth_contra with eta = log(r'/d)/2.
wl-power-window: The Lean proves this in two steps: windowHyp_of_rpow gives Deduction.WindowHyp in the variable y with R(y) = |C| y^theta, and windowHypU_of_windowHyp changes variables. The text takes R(u) = |C| e^(theta u) directly. The argument works for any function in place of G_F.
wl-zero-free-family: zeroFree_of_rpow_window is lemmaL composed with windowHyp_of_rpow. Its conclusion, ZeroFree F theta, says that LFunction (chi i) s != 0 for every s with Re s > theta; for the trivial character modulo 1 this includes s = 1, where Mathlib gives riemannZeta a finite nonzero value. lemmaL treats Re s >= 1 separately by the nonvanishing there, which the text does not need.
wl-windows: Formalism.HC.HasWindows S la. For a family, FamCore.Windows la is HasWindows of its set of scales (windows_iff).
wl-zero-free-level: This is UpperTheory.Comparison₂.formB, which proves Level.FormB, that is, Level.FormBAt la for every la > 1. The family is UpperTheory.Comparison₂.level_family, with weight 1 at PChar.one and Level.wt elsewhere; level_family_adm shows that a primitive trivial character has N = 1.
wl-families: Formalism.HC.level_of_tiedWin and zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin_cyc are stated for an arbitrary type family Fam : R -> Type 1, a map core from Fam eps to Formalism.MainNotions.FamCore eps and an arbitrary predicate Tied; the situation describes these data. The set of scales is FamCore.Win, the members at x are FamCore.Ix x with data D x i (a definite-side datum, Formalism.BasicNotions.D7), 'satisfies the host conditions for K' is Formalism.HC.EFamC (built from EAt, that is, EAtH of Chapter 3), and 'tied on its scales' is ChebyshevInequalityOnFamilyWindows. FamCore has many further fields that this chapter does not use. In Chapter 13 the data are FamP, toFamCore and ChainTied.
wl-family-conditions: Condition (1) is Formalism.HC.ChebyshevInequalityOnWindows and condition (2) is Formalism.HC.ChebyshevInequalityAtWindowScale.
wl-level-from-windows: Condition (3) is the hypothesis hB : Level.FormBAt la, which formB discharges for la > 1; level_of_tiedWin itself needs no hypothesis on la. The choice of epsilon is exists_small_eps, and the exponent theta = 1/2 + min(Re s - 1/2, 1/2)/2 is the one in the Lean proof.
wl-zero-free-cyclic: zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin_cyc concludes ZeroFreeOn Q, that is, PChar.ZeroFreeAbove psi (1/2) for every psi with Q psi. It goes through zeroFreeOn_of_tiedWin and zeroFreeOn_of_levels. Condition (3) is the hypothesis hB, (Level.cyc psi).FormB.
wl-supply: In UpperTheory.Top.zeroFreeAll_of_topG the corollary is applied with Fam = FamP, core = toFamCore, Tied = ChainTied and Q the set of all primitive characters. Condition (1) is UpperTheory.Comparison₂.level_gm_le_on_family_scales, condition (3) is formB, and condition (2) is assembled from TopG, the host existence hypothesis HostExW and eFamC_of_cls. The value la = 3/2 is fixed where zeroFreeAll_of_topG is used (EveryCharacter.lean).
